idiom_name: hand-written fork/forward: forward, then a nonblocking copy to an AF_UNIX socketpair tap fd with EAGAIN drop counting
implementation_notes: C has no messaging or EIP layer, so the tap is hand-written inside the channel: the channel keeps a second destination fd and every send writes the original to the primary, then writes the same bytes to the tap. Create the tap once with socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_SEQPACKET | SOCK_NONBLOCK, 0, tap) and hand tap[1] to the analyzer (a forked child or a second thread's poll loop); SOCK_SEQPACKET preserves message boundaries so the analyzer recv()s whole messages with no framing, and the write into the socket buffer is the copy point - once send() returns, the kernel owns the tapped bytes, so the analyzer can never alias or mutate what the primary path still uses. Blocking semantics are the whole design: send()/write() block by default whenever the tap's socket/pipe buffer is full, which would let a stalled analyzer stall the primary flow, so the tap fd MUST be O_NONBLOCK (or the call use MSG_DONTWAIT) and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK is the explicit overflow signal - count it in a visible drop counter and move on; never retry inline. EPIPE means the analyzer detached: close the tap fd and keep forwarding (send with MSG_NOSIGNAL so the dead reader does not raise SIGPIPE). The same shape works over a plain pipe - a byte stream with a 64 KiB default capacity that fcntl F_SETPIPE_SZ can raise - when the analyzer tolerates re-framing. For a named, pollable queue use a second POSIX message queue instead: mq_open it with bounded mq_maxmsg/mq_msgsize, set O_NONBLOCK via mq_setattr, and mq_send returns EAGAIN when the analyzer is behind (EMSGSIZE over mq_msgsize), which is the drop point; note the Linux default ceilings are only 10 messages and 8192 bytes unless /proc/sys/fs/mqueue/* is raised. If the channel already rides ZeroMQ, the library owns the tap: zmq_proxy(frontend, backend, capture) sends every message received on both sockets to the capture socket, which must be ZMQ_PUB, ZMQ_DEALER, ZMQ_PUSH or ZMQ_PAIR - choose ZMQ_PUB for the capture because a slow subscriber then silently drops at the high water mark (best-effort, tap-safe), while PUSH/DEALER captures block the proxy when muted, which violates the never-block-the-primary invariant. tee(2) is the literal in-kernel tap for pure byte streams: it duplicates pipe bytes to another pipe without consuming the input (splice(2) then consumes it), fails EAGAIN under SPLICE_F_NONBLOCK, and accepts pipes only.
pitfalls: Tap writes block by default: send() blocks when the tap socket's send buffer is full and write() blocks on a full pipe, so a slow analyzer stalls the primary sender unless the tap fd is O_NONBLOCK or MSG_DONTWAIT is used - and then the loss policy is EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK (POSIX allows both constants; check both).

EINTR is not an error to ignore: write()/send() fail with EINTR when a signal arrives before any byte is transferred, and a blocked write can also return a partial write - retry the primary path on EINTR, but on a nonblocking tap treat EINTR as a counted drop, not a stall.

If every read end of the tap is closed, write() raises SIGPIPE, whose default disposition kills the flow you were tapping; use send() with MSG_NOSIGNAL (EPIPE is still returned) or ignore SIGPIPE, and close redundant tap fd duplicates after fork(2) so EPIPE is actually delivered when the analyzer exits.

A POSIX mqueue tap is silently undersized by default: mq_send() blocks on a full queue unless O_NONBLOCK is set via mq_setattr, and Linux ceilings applied at mq_open() default to mq_maxmsg = 10 and mq_msgsize = 8192 bytes (/proc/sys/fs/mqueue/msg_max, msgsize_max), so real payloads fail EMSGSIZE and the queue drains to EAGAIN drops unless the limits are raised deliberately.

zmq_proxy() capture is constrained and asymmetric: the capture socket must be ZMQ_PUB, ZMQ_DEALER, ZMQ_PUSH or ZMQ_PAIR (a PULL/SUB capture is a misuse the proxy does not diagnose), and only ZMQ_PUB drops silently at a subscriber's high water mark - ZMQ_PUSH/ZMQ_DEALER captures block on zmq_send() when muted, feeding the analyzer's slowness back into the proxy.
